evidence_grade_key.measured_on_engine: Reported from a test on a real engine or combustor.
evidence_grade_key.vendor_claim: Manufacturer press release, patent or technical paper without independent data.
evidence_grade_key.cycle_simulation: Thermodynamic or process simulation in a peer-reviewed or agency report.
evidence_grade_key.review_statement: A review or white paper quoting others.

provenance.verbatim_flag_key: verbatim = number printed in the source at the stated location; derived = arithmetic by this agent from printed numbers (formula given); search_summary = number seen only in a search-tool summary of an abstract, source page not opened (treated as unverified)
provenance.page_note: PDF page numbers are the file page; printed page in brackets where it differs.

key_deliverable_efficiency_difference.quantity: Combined-cycle efficiency with hydrogen-rich cracked gas (H2/N2) minus combined-cycle efficiency with ammonia fired directly, comparable machines
key_deliverable_efficiency_difference.unit: percentage points (positive = cracked gas better), LHV basis on the ammonia (or hydrogen) energy supplied

like_for_like_values.detail: full cracking (alpha = 0), exhaust-heated cracker, about 54 % versus vaporised NH3 case 2a 49.12 %, same 43 MW-class machine, PR 8

like_for_like_values.delta_pp: up to 5.0 to 5.5 (unit printed as per cent; abstract says 5.5, conclusion says 5)
like_for_like_values.detail: chemically recuperated cycle (cracked gas, exhaust-heated) versus simple cycle without recuperation, ammonia fed, TIT 800 to 1200 degC

not_like_for_like_values.detail: 66.9 % (hydrogen, steam-diluted, Exhibit 4-9) minus 59.6 % (ammonia, Exhibit 4-6), same agency method and baseline, but pure H2 with steam injection, no cracker, no N2 in the fuel; an upper bound, not a cracked-gas figure

MHI patent: cracked-gas plant about 97.4 % of natural-gas gross efficiency, with natural gas 63 % or more (so about -1.6 pp versus gas) minus NETL ammonia 59.6 minus 61.0 (-1.4 pp versus gas). Two unrelated machines, gross versus net basis, vendor claim versus agency model: indicative only and not a valid difference

recommended_range_for_modellers.supported_range_pp: +4.9 to +5.5 (two independent simulation groups, direction and size agree)
recommended_range_for_modellers.sensitivity_range_pp: 0 to +5.5 (lower bound 0 reflects the cross-source vendor reading, which is not a like-for-like comparison)
recommended_range_for_modellers.evidence_strength: Weak to moderate. Every number is a cycle simulation (no measured combined-cycle data on cracked gas or on ammonia). Only two like-for-like comparisons exist, both on small or idealised machines (43 MW-class at pressure ratio 8; HYSYS cycle at 800-1200 degC inlet), neither on an F- or H-class machine. The sign is consistent (cracked gas better when the cracker is heated by turbine exhaust); the size is not established for a large frame machine, where direct ammonia is modelled to lose only about 1.4 pp against natural gas (NETL, redesigned turbine).

entries.machine_or_study: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries / Mitsubishi Power
entries.status: Development announced 1 Mar 2021 of a 40 MW-class, 100 % ammonia gas turbine in the H-25 series, SCR plus newly developed combustor, 'commercialization in or around 2025' subject to testing. MHI Technical Review 62(3), 2025: ammonia single-fired system and a high-efficiency SCR for medium and small gas turbines are being developed and verified; H-25 (above 40 MW) 100 % H2 dry firing verification ongoing; M501JAC verified at 30 vol% H2 on actual equipment. No published H-25 ammonia efficiency or NOx figure and no evidence of a commercial delivery found.

entries.machine_or_study: IHI and GE Vernova
entries.status: 18 Mar 2026: full-scale combustor components fired on 100 % ammonia at F-class full-load pressure, temperature and flow at IHI's Aioi test facility; no numeric emissions or efficiency published ('align with the companies' development roadmap'); goal commercial 100 % ammonia F-class turbine by 2030. IHI earlier ran a 2 MW class turbine on ammonia-methane (NETL 2024 p. 17, SCR needed).

entries.machine_or_study: Siemens Energy
entries.status: No source found in this search for a Siemens Energy ammonia-fired gas turbine test or product. Not recorded as absent from the world, only as not found.

entries.machine_or_study: Halim, Zain and Khoo (2025), Applied Energy 386, 125581
entries.status: Full text NOT accessible (A*STAR repository lists the file apen-125581.pdf as request-a-copy only; publisher page not tried beyond DOI). Abstract read at the repository and IDEAS. The quoted figures 60.1 MW, LCOH 15.1 (green) and 10.1 (blue) USD/kg, 'direct combustion about 40 per cent cheaper' and '30 to 60 vol% H2 for the H-25' are NOT found in the abstract and cannot be located. The abstract does say direct ammonia use is economically preferable to cracking because of cracking capital and operating cost.
